Commentary.Commentary: What do Australia have to do now? They have around 137 overs to bat out on a wicket which is turning and bouncing. Also, looking at their track record against spin in recent times, this is surely not going to be easy. They will have to take it session by session and their first test will be to battle out today's overs with not much damage. Pakistan, on the flip side, will rely on their spinners to do the damage for them. Sarfraz will want a repeat of their first innings' performance. Will they run through the visitors' batting line-up once again or will the Aussies put up a fight? Join us soon to find out.

Right then, Australia have been set a target of 462. A massive task ahead for them. Pakistan entered into the third innings with a huge lead of 280. They did lose 3 quick wickets yesterday but the 65-run partnership between Imam and Sohail took their lead close to 400 before the two fell in quick succession this morning. Azam and Shafiq then added another handy stand, 71 to be precise, to take it past 450. The Pakistan side did not bat for long after the Lunch break. They looked for some quick runs, got them through Asad Shafiq and once he got out, they declared.

OUT! Holes out at the deep mid-wicket fence. Pakistan have declared on 181/6. Shafiq tries to get under this full pitch ball on off and whack it over deep mid-wicket from within his crease. He cannot get enough timing and power on it to cross the rope and the man positioned near the boundary line, Mitchell Marsh, takes an easy catch with fingers pointing upwards.
Very full on middle, flicked to short mid-wicket.
FOUR! Reverse sweep has come out now. Shafiq sees the line outside off and the length was also full to play that shot to perfection, it beats the short third man fielder to cross the boundary there.
Stays back to this flatter one around off and punches it straight to the lone fielder inside the ring on the off side at covers.
Starts with a flighted ball outside off and turning into the right-hander, Asad comes forward in defense.
Floats it up on middle, the batsman keeps it out.
Once again the negative line, pitches it outside leg, gets this one to turn away sharply. Asad is squared up as he tries to defend but manages to keep it out towards point for a run.
Once again makes room but Holland follows him, Shafiq nudges it to short fine leg.

Brings the reverse sweep out and plays it well. Does not try to hit it too hard, he just guides it through backward point and bags a brace. Shafiq seems to have stepped on the gas here, has shown good attacking intent in the last few overs.
Uses his feet and eases it through mid on for a run.
Flatter on the leg pole, Azam pushes it back to the bowler.
Tossed up again around off, Shafiq solidly defends it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Asad rocks onto the back foot to this shortish ball and punches the ball to covers.

SIX! BOOM! And the maximum has brought up 3,000 runs for Shafiq at the No. 6 position, becomes the first batsman to reach this feat for Pakistan. Lyon tosses this up again, Shafiq this time takes on the bait, skips down the track and whacks it through the line and with the spin over the long on fence for a huge one. Pakistan starting to press the accelerator.

Leg bye! Wonderful off spin bowling this by Lyon, he flights this one up and lands it full and outside off, turning into Azam who is looking to block it but the ball spins in, misses his bat and hits his pads to get deflected into the point region and they steal a leg bye.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Bye! Jon fires this way down the leg side to even beat his skipper behind, the batsman take a bye.
Very full on leg, the batsman works it down the leg side.
Azam tries to play at it but due to the angle from way outside leg he gets hit on the pads. Negative tactics from the Aussies these?
This time he tries to steal a run by turning it into the leg side but finds the fielder at backward square leg.
Similar line and length, Babar comes forward and opens up a bit to defend it.
Tossed up and full from over the stumps as he looks to pitch it in the rough outside the leg stump of the right-hander, Babar keeps it out off the front foot.
Fuller and slower on off, kept out.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Asad dances down the track with some good aggressive intent, does not reach to the pitch of it, decides to defend it.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Goes back to this floated delivery a bit outside off and just softly taps it into the point region to get Shafiq on strike.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground. No rush still.
Azam gets down and plays a sweep shot. One run added to the total.
Shafiq gets back and across to this shorter in length ball on middle and flicks it to mid-wicket to get another run.
Skips down the track does Azam and drives it crisply to long on for a single.
Much fuller ball, and this length is much easier to drive as Shafiq does exactly that towards mid on and gets off strike.
A bit wide this of off, Shafiq decides to leave it at the very last moment.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Azam is happy to block this tossed up ball on off. Doesn't seem as if Pakistan are eager to score quickly, or should they give themselves some more time?
Azam dances down the track but decides to defend as he is not to the pitch of the ball.
Stays back to this slower and shorter in length delivery, blocks it out from his crease.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and onto the ground.
Shafiq lets the ball come under his bat and then pushes it to covers to take a run and bring the 50-run stand up.
Shafiq nicely comes forward to defend this full length ball on off.
Nathan Lyon to bowl from the other end.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flighted and fuller, driven to long on to jog across to the other end.
Shorter in length this,  punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Beaten! Much better from Holland, he loops it a bit more and lands it full around of, Asad plays at it but misses due to the away spin on the ball.
Errs in length again as he keeps it short and outside off, Asad waits for it to arrive close and cuts with a slightly open face to find the gap at backward point and gets a brace.
Short and wide of off to start after Lunch, Babar cuts it through point to get things going and gets off strike.

The umpires and the Aussie team are seen making their way out to the middle as we are about to commence the afternoon session. The Pakistan batting pair of Babar Azam and Asad Shafiq also stride out to the center with the former on strike having taken a single off the last ball before Lunch. Jon Holland to start proceedings for Australia. Let's play...
... DAY 4, AFTERNOON SESSION ...

What will we see after the break? Pakistan coming out in the T20 mode, adding a few quick runs and then declaring? Or will they keep on batting to tire out the Australians physically and mentally? Join us in a short while to find out.

Imam and Sohail started the day off cautiously but once the two got their eye in, then attacked the bowlers. The former was dropped by Head but then looked very fluent throughout. He was unfortunate to miss out on a half ton by just 2 runs. The opener along with Haris added a 65-run stand which more or less has batted Australia out of the game. The visitors did manage to pick the two set batsmen in quick succession but that came too late.

This session - 33.4 overs, 110 runs and 2 wickets. Another session which was dominated by the hosts. They managed to score freely and lost only two wickets. The lead is now nearing the 450-run mark and it will be interesting to find out when Pakistan will declare.
Extra bounce on this one! Flatter and outside off, Azam stands tall and guides it through point for a single to end this session. LUNCH ON DAY 4!
Flatter outside off, Azam cuts it through point for a couple.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Floats it up on middle, Azam defends it.
Works it with the angle towards the leg side and hands over the strike to Azam.
Flatter again on off, it turns away. Shafiq tries to defend but the ball takes the edge and goes towards point.
Marnus Labuschagne comes back into the attack.

Now it is slightly short and outside off, AS guides it towards point. It is in between the two fielders there. Mitchell Marsh at backward point dives full stretch to his right and stops it. Saves three for his side.
FOUR! Lovely shot! Runs now coming thick and fast here! 150 up for Pakistan. The lead is now 430. On the pads, Shafiq goes down on one knee quickly and sweeps it through square leg for a boundary.
Uses his feet and strokes it towards long on for another single.
A low full toss on middle, Shafiq times it down to long on for a single.
Gives it air around off, the batsman keeps it out.
Top edge but safe! Goes for a sweep to a ball which is way outside off. It takes the top edge and lands safely in the short fine leg region for a brace.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
This time he waits that bit more for the ball to come closer to him and flicks it behind square leg to pick a run and get off strike.
Similar delivery and identical flick shot into the square leg region by Shafiq.
Slower and shorter this on middle, turned into the leg side off the back foot.
Well bowled, he sensed the batsman will charge down and pulls his length back, Asad does exactly that, cannot reach to the pitch of the ball and has to lunge a bit more forward to block it out.
Continues to give it air and keep it full, Babar quickly skips down the track and drives this thorough mid on for a single.
Floats it up wide outside off, Shafiq shoulders arms to it.
On the stumps, kept out.
Wide outside off, left alone.
Shafiq now steps down the track and makes it into a full toss. He eases it down to long on for a brace. Good running!
On the pads, Azam flicks it fine on the leg side for a run.
Dances down the track and tries to work it across the line but gets a soft leading edge towards short covers.

Flatter and quicker on off, Babar stays back and cleverly opens the face of the bat to use the pace on the ball and guide it towards the third man region. The ball though stops before the rope there and Starc picks it up and throws it back to the keeper. The batsmen have finished running three.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Tosses this up a bit more, searching for some extra spin, but cannot get it as Azam blocks it off the front foot.
Gives himself some room, Babar, seeing this short and wide of off delivery, then he punches to covers but cannot find the gap.
Tosses this one up just to vary his length, Babar is up to the task as he lunges forward in a rock solid defense.
Keeps it a bit shorter in length, seeing the length, Babar goes back and turns it into the leg side.
Flatter and outside off, the batsman slaps it through covers for another single.
Uses his feet and drives it nicely but finds covers.
FOUR! Short and put away! A half-tracker outside off, the batsman cuts it through point and the ball races away to the fence.
The batsman has driven it through mid off.
Another floated ball outside off, it is timed through covers for a run.
Loopy ball on off, it is driven through covers for a run.
Very full on middle, jammed out to mid on.
Gives it air on off, the batsman blocks it out.

FOUR! Class! Not easy to play an offie through the off side especially on a turning wicket. Lyon floats it up around off, he bowls it a touch too full. Shafiq reaches out to it and drives it through covers for a boundary.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Floats it up around off, Shafiq is solid in defense.
Well played again! Uses his feet but does not get to the pitch of it, adjusts well and with soft hands works it to short leg.
Another loopy ball on off, Shafiq pushes it towards covers for a run.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region. One run added to the total.
Flatter on off, Azam guides it towards point.
Flighted ball on off, Azam blocks it out.

SIX! All the way! Maybe he has decided to play the attacking way to get back into form. Dances down the track, does not quite get to the pitch of the ball but still goes through with the shot. Connects well and it goes over the long on fence for a biggie. 400 is the lead now. How many more will Pakistan want to add?
A little short by Holland, the batsman goes back and punches it through covers for a run.
Now uses his feet to good use as he dances down the track and flicks it through mid-wicket for a run.
Floats it up on off, Shafiq shows great technique by playing it late, with soft hands and onto the ground.
With the turn, Shafiq works it towards short leg.
Flighted ball around off, Shafiq reaches out for it and keeps it out.
Slightly short on off, the batsman keeps it out.
Plays it well! The ball there bounced and also turned back in, Shafiq with soft hands works it fine down the leg side for a couple. Gets off the mark with that.
Nathan Lyon is back into the attack.
Tossed up ball in line with the stumps, Babar has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
In no hurry is Azam as he comes forward to defend this loopy ball on off from the front foot.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Again a flighted and slower delivery on middle and off, the right-hander taking his time to settle down and keeps it out.

Again keeps it full looking for some turn, however he is not able to get the same amount of spin against the right-hander as there is not much rough there, Babar blocks this full ball off the front foot.
Jon Holland continues with his tail up and bowls a tossed up ball on off, Babar comes forward in a solid defense.
Times it through covers and gets to the other end.
Floats it up on middle, kept out.
Babar Azam walks in to bat.

OUT! Three reds and Sohail has to walk back! Excellent use of technology. Labuschagne gets his first of this innings and second of the match. He was picked for his batting but he has done a better job with the ball. It is another shorter delivery outside off, Haris goes back to pull but the ball does not bounce as Sohail expected it to. He misses it to get hit near the thigh pad. The players let out a loud appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Paine walks up to his bowler and after a chat, he goes for the review. Time for the replays and they show that the on-field call has to be overturned. The height ain't an issue and it's hitting the leg stump. Wickets in quick succession for Australia and Pakistan now have half the side back in the hut.
A huge appeal but it has been turned down! Paine has a chat and then reviews it. Height maybe an issue here.
Floats it up on off, kept out.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Shorter around off, Sohail punches it towards covers.
Asad Shafiq is the new man in.

OUT! Caught and bowled! Imam misses out on consecutive half tons! A soft dismissal there. Imam dances down the track like he has been doing throughout his innings. Does not get to the pitch of the ball though. Holland gets it to land around the rough area outside off and the ball turns back in. Imam tries to push it towards the off side but ends up chipping it back to the bowler who accepts an easy catch. Holland gets his third scalp, ending the 65-run stand. However, the partnership has taken the lead close to the 400-run mark.
Sohail flicks it through square leg and gives Imam the strike.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Uses his feet and strokes it down to long on for a run.
Flicks it fine with the turn through short fine leg for a run.
Tosses it up on middle, Sohail pushes it back to the bowler.
Another one on the pads, the batsman flicks it towards fine leg for a quick run.
Tosses this up but it is on the pads, Imam flicks it through square leg for a single.
Short again on middle, Haris pushes it down to long on and jogs to the other end.
Good amount of turn there but it is very short outside off, comes back in. Imam pushes it towards covers for a run.
Quicker again on the pads, the batsman goes back and works it towards short fine leg. Bowling very quick here is the leg spinner.
Flatter delivery on the pads, the batsman works it to mid-wicket.
Marnus Labuschagne is into the attack. Australia are trying everything here to break this partnership.
A dot to end! A maiden by Lyon. He darts it on off, Sohail keeps it out. Not a lot of balls have turned today for Lyon. Maybe due to the pace Lyon is bowling at.
A little too full this time on off, it is driven back to the bowler.
Flatter on the pads, Sohail with the angle works it to mid-wicket.
Again around off, it goes on with the arm. Sohail defends it.
On the stumps, no real sign of any turn as Sohail defends it with utmost ease.
Slower through the air around off, Sohail prods forward and blocks it.
On middle, Imam gets right behind the line of the delivery and dead-bats it.
Nicely played! It is floated on the pads, Imam tucks it through square leg, it is in the gap in that region and the batsmen get two.
Slightly shorter in length, Sohail with the turn works it to mid-wicket for a run.
Another tossed up ball on off, Sohail blocks it out.
Imam dances down the track and eases it to long on for a run. 100 up for Pakistan, the lead now is 20 short of 400.
Jon comes from around the wicket to the left-hander, maybe to create a natural angle away from the batter. Tosses it up around off, the batsman keeps it out.
Jon Holland is back on.
Another tossed up ball on off, Sohail blocks it onto the ground.
Another loopy ball on middle, Sohail defends it out.
On the stumps, HS is solid in defense.
Slightly shorter around off, Sohail waits for it and then guides it to point.
Flatter delivery on off, Sohail pushes it to covers.
A little too much on the leg side, Imam plants his front foot forward and then flicks it through mid-wicket for an easy single.
Change of ends for Nathan Lyon.

Drinks. Pakistan have marched along well and have swollen their lead to 378 runs without losing any wickets today. They may now look to up the ante a bit and score some quick runs before declaring their innings. Australia have nothing going their way. There is spin on offer but both their tweakers have failed to leave any impact. The dropped catch didn't help their cause either. Things clearly looking glum for them.

FOUR! Drags his length short this time and Sohail picks the length up early, rocks back and pulls it hard through the mid-wicket region to get a boundary off the last ball before drinks. 50-run stand is up now, Pakistan lead by 378!
Similar ball to Imam this time, he too drives this through mid on to get off strike.
Very full this in line with the leg stump, Sohail drives it to long on and gets a single.
Full and straight again, blocked off the front foot again.
Similar ball and defends off the front foot by the southpaw. Don't think he will take any undue risk just before the drinks break.
A very full and slow delivery to start off with, Sohail blocks it off the front foot.
Travis Head is into the attack.
Starc bangs this last ball of the over a bit shorter and angling into Imam. The opener swivels well and pulls it through backward square leg to pick up a brace and take this stand now to 47 runs.
An identical delivery and a similar defense off the front foot by Imam.
Immaculate line and length this from the quick left-hand pacer, Imam blocks it coming forward.
A bit fuller and on a good length on middle and off, kept out off the front foot by Imam.
On a good length around off, well defended off the front foot by the left-handed opener.
Fast and full angling into the batsman, the angle though is a bit too much as the ball strays down the leg side, Imam tries flicking it but misses.
Quicker ball to end the over. The line is outside off which allows Sohail time to leave it watchfully.
Slower and on off, Sohail leans ahead and defends.
Defended off the front foot by the southpaw presenting the full face of the bat.
Flighted ball on off, Sohail comes forward to block it out.
Tossed up on middle, Haris lunges forward in defense.
Skips down the track to this loopy delivery on off and drives this to long on to take the lead to 370 with this single.
Comes back to a good length around off, Sohail blocks it off the back foot from within his crease.
Similar line and length but this time Sohail opens the bat face slightly to drive it through cover-point for a couple.
On a good length but a bit outside off, driven softly on the up to covers.
Better from Starc as he lands this one on a good length around off, Sohail keeps it out from his crease.
Fuller than the previous one this, almost a yorker on middle and off, blocked out off the front foot by Haris.
Very full and attacking the stumps, Sohail drives this gently to the fielder at short mid on, positioned just beside the pitch.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot back down the ground.
Much quicker and flatter just outside off, left at the very last moment by the southpaw.
Not that short to go back and play it to the off side but that is exactly what Imam did here. Somehow punches it out towards point.
Tossed up on middle, defended off the front foot with the bat well in front of the pads.
Similar length but a bit wide of off this, Imam rocks back and across and cuts it straight to backward point.
Quicker and bit shorter than full length on middle and off, Imam goes back in defense.
On a good length again, Sohail keeps it out off from within the crease.
Lands this on a good length and wide of off, Sohail shoulders arms.
Fast and full on middle, Imam flicks it through square leg to get a single and get off strike.

FOUR! EDGY BOUNDARY! Again a full ball just outside off, Imam goes for the cover drive a bit away from his body. The ball though takes the outside edge and flies very low through the vacant first slip region for a boundary.
Dishes this much fuller and attacking the stumps, Imam drives it crisply to mid off.
Starc starts today with a short of a good length ball on off, Imam defends from his crease.
Mitchell Starc is into the attack.
A bit shorter this, Sohail goes back to punch it to cover-point where the fielder makes a good diving stop.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Very full on off, kept out easily.
A bit slower this on off, Sohail has to wait a bit longer before blocking it off the front foot.
Similar ball and an identical defense offered by Sohail.
Tossed up around middle and off, Haris lunges forward in defense.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Drifts down the leg again and Sohail turns it into the fine leg region to change strike. Pakistan doing it easy here.
Fuller and quicker on his pads, flicked to mid-wicket.
A bit shorter this, Sohail rocks back and punches it through mid off to get a brace.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

SIX! BANG! Skips down the track on the very first ball and smashes this over the long on fense to bring up the second biggie of the morning. Sohail doing it well here, he is taking Pakistan to safer shores very quickly.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Charges down the track looking to block it. He does not reach to the pitch of the ball as it spins and bounces to take a slight leading edge. Falls just short of Lyon.
Shorter again and Imam again punches this to mid on off the back foot.
Fuller again in line with the stumps, Imam prods forward in defense.
A bit shorter which allows Imam to go back in his crease and punch it to cover-point.
Tossed up on middle and off, defended off the front foot.
Due to the last delivery, Holland bowls this flatter around off, Sohail stays inside the crease and defends it out.
FOUR! Up and over! Maybe this is the way to play on this surface. Sohail skips down the track to the flighted ball and lofts it over mid off for a boundary. The lead is now 350.

Sharp turn! With the ball turning in and so sharply, there should be a backward short leg place. That is how Australia got one of their wickets. Holland floats it up outside off, it pitches and spins back in sharply. Sohail tries to defend but the ball goes off the inner half, uppishly through the vacant backward short leg region and towards short fine leg.
Flatter around off, Sohail reaches out to the delivery and keeps it out.
Another loopy ball on off, Sohail prods forward and defends it.
Once again uses his feet and flicks it with the turn through square leg for a run.
Fires it on off, the batsman keeps it out.
Works it off his pads to the leg side but straight towards the fielder behind square leg.
On the stumps, the batsman keeps it out.
Bowls this one quicker and on middle, Imam tries to defend but the ball goes off the inner half towards square leg for an easy run.

FOUR! Goes inside out and gets the desired result. Imam is quick on his feet, gets to the pitch of the ball and also makes room. He lofts it over covers and the ball goes for a boundary. Moves to 30, Imam.
Gives it air around off, Imam lunges and keeps it out.
Tossed up ball on off, Sohail comes forward in defense. End of an eventful over.
Fullish and on middle, driven straight back and it went on to hit the stumps at the bowler's head.
Tossed up ball on middle, Imam draws forward with a big stride to defend but it takes the inner half of the bat and goes uppishly but wide of the right side of the short leg fielder. A single taken.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Is it a drop? Replays show, it is. The reaction of the bowler says that it has just about carried to the man at silly mid on. Imam drives this full ball straight, it goes flat and low to Travis Head beside the pitch on the leg side but he fails to hold onto it. Tough chance but should have been taken. The Aussies need to take these catches to come back in this match.
A bit flatter on the middle and leg line, Sohail flicks it through square leg to get off strike.
Shorter in line with the stumps, Sohail flicks it off the back foot into mid-wicket to get a single.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
A bit shorter in length and it allows the batsman time to rock back and punch it through covers to get a brace.
Tossed up ball on off, turning away. Sohail does well to account for the spin and keeps it out.
Sohail gets behind the line of this fuller delivery on off and blocks it.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Beaten! Goes for the expansive drive through covers, tries reaching the ball away from his body and misses it completely. Paine also fumbles behind to allow the pair to run through for a bye.
Fuller and slower ball on middle is driven to mid on.
Imam quickly goes back and pushes it into the cover-point region to get a run.
Full delivery on the pads, Imam flicks it to mid-wicket.
Slower and shorter then full length, Sohail punches this into covers to get off strike.

SIX! WOW! Where did that come from? First aggressive intent shown by Pakistan today. He seems to be continuing from where he left off in the first innings. Jon gives this a bit more air and seeing that, Haris skips down the track and whacks it over long on for a maximum. Went with the spin and fetched a biggie for himself. Lead is now 335.
Shorter and a bit wide of off, Imam punches it to covers.
Flighted loopy ball on off, Imam blocks it off the front foot.
Haris reaches to the pitch of the ball and drives it to long on for a single.
Sohail has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
He pulls his length back a bit and makes Haris stay back and block it out off the back foot.
Tossed up on off, Sohail defends off the front foot.
Again a very full delivery to end the over, the southpaw keeps it out off the front foot.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Similar ball and defended off the front foot by Imam.
A bit too full this by Jon as Imam comes forward and smothers the spin.
Fuller on off, Haris drives it with the turn to long on and gets off strike.
Bowls this very full in line with the stumps, it's kept out off the front foot by Sohail.
Flighted delivery on off, Imam stays back and defends from his crease.
The southpaw lets the ball go outside his off stump.

Beaten! That is an excellent ball from Nathan as he gives it a bit more rip. The ball lands on off and spins away sharply to beat the outside edge of Imam's bat. There was some sound as the ball passed the willow but none of the Australian fielders appealed. Replays show that the ball missed the bat by quite a distance, not sure though from where the sound came...
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
A bit slower and shorter, Imam flicks it to square leg.
The offie starts from around the wicket and lands this on a fuller length on middle and off line, Imam blocks off the front foot.
Nathan Lyon to bowl from the other end.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
A bit fuller on off, flicked by the southpaw to mid-wicket to get his first run of the day.
Flighted on off, blocked off the front foot.
Starts with a tossed up ball on off, Sohail drives it to long on to get off the mark.
The players are on the field. The Pakistan duo of Imam-ul-Haq and Haris Sohail stride out to the center with the former to face the first ball. Let's go...

Brendon Julian is taking Jon Holland's interview. The spinner expresses his disappointment over Australia's batting collapse and considers that it wasn't ideal. Admits that as a team they are disappointed with their effort with the bat. States they have got some plans in place for today and will look to execute it. Reckons the wicket has started to spin a bit more from the rough than the first two days. Mentions that the plan is to pick quick wickets and then hope to bat well in the fourth innings.

If the first two days crawled forward at the speed of a snail, yesterday saw this game sprint ahead like a cheetah. Wickets fell like nine pins post the Lunch break on Day 3 with Australia experiencing a sorry collapse. After gaining a massive 280-run lead, Pakistan are in a strong position, even after the loss of 3 wickets. They have the upper hand and would try to bat Australia out of this Test match. The Aussies, on the flip side, will hope to bowl out the hosts as soon as possible and then be optimistic about their chances with the bat. The first session today will determine if the Kangaroos have any chance of getting back in this game. Stay tuned...
... DAY 4, MORNING SESSION ...

Now then, 13 wickets fell today which means the track that appeared to be a road for the first two days has opened up. These are not good signs for Australia as they will be batting last. The hosts won't mind that at all as they already have a big lead in their pocket. Pakistan would now look to add another 100-150 runs and then hope for a repeat performance from their bowlers. What do we have in store for us on Day 4? Join us at 0600 GMT (1000 local) to find out.

Day 3 started off with Finch and Khawaja milking the Pakistan bowlers. The first session was a wicket-less one for the visitors with the duo putting together a century stand. However, it all changed after the break. From 142 for 0, the Aussies slipped miserably and got bundled out for 202, courtesy Bilal Asif and Mohammad Abbas' magnificent bowling. The pair picked up all the 10 wickets between them with the debutant bagging a 6-fer and the latter finishing with four.

End of a great day of a Test match! Australia ended it well but they are still way behind the 8-ball. They headed into Pakistan's second innings after conceding a lead of 280. Wickets were the demand of the hour for them and they have got three of them. However, Pakistan are still on top as they have extended their lead to 325 runs and still have a lot of batting to come.

OUT! Judicious use of the review by Australia as they have struck in the last over of the day. Another failure for Ali. Holland gets his second. This is tossed up around the leg pole. It pitches and then straightens. Ali tries to keep it out but misses. The ball hits him on the front pad and the players appeal. The umpire does not agree. Paine walks up to his bowler and after a chat signals the 'T'. The replays roll in and firstly they confirm that there is no bat. Hawk-Eye then shows the ball to be pitching in line and hitting the stumps. Three reds and Azhar is given his marching orders. Also, with that wicket, it's time for Stumps on Day 3.
Review time! An appeal for an LBW against Ali has been turned down. Paine wants it to be referred. Pitching looks to be an issue.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They have run through for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground. Last over of the day coming up.
Bowls it very quick on middle, Ali gets his bat down in time and keeps it out.
FOUR! Swept and swept fine! Goes down on one knee and sweeps it through backward square leg region and the ball races away.
Dances down the track again but Lyon fires it wide outside off. Ali reaches out for it and puts bat on ball.
Dances down the track and times it to long off and gets to the other end.
Pitches it on off, Imam pushes it to covers.
Slower through the air outside off, the batsman shoulders arms to it.
The batsman gets to the pitch of the ball and connects.
Dances down the track and strokes it towards the cover fielder.
Slower through the air outside off, Ali watches it closely and lets it be.
Very full on off, Ali jams it out.
Uses his feet and eases this down to long on for a run.
Azhar Ali strides out to the center.

OUT! The move to send the nightwatchman has not worked. Two wickets in two overs for Australia. Lyon gets his first. He tosses this up around off, it turns back in sharply. Bilal prods forward and tries to defend but the ball hits the inside edge and goes towards backward short leg. Travis Head there takes a sharp low catch.
Flatter around off, goes on with the arm. The batter defends it off the back foot.
Another tossed up ball, the batsman lunges and defends.
Like that! Loopy ball on off, Bilal blocks it out.
Fires it on middle, Imam flicks it through mid-wicket for a run. Lyon is a touch short here. He needs to toss it up a little more and land it full.
Flatter delivery on off, Imam punches it to covers.
Tosses it up outside off, left alone.
Bilal Asif is the new batsman in. A second nightwatchman of the match for Pakistan.

OUT! An excellent catch there by Labuschagne. He showed good reflexes. It was on middle and it turns away and also sticks in the surface. Hafeez tries to play it against the turn which is never a good idea on a turning wicket. The ball takes the leading edge and hits the body of the silly point fielder. Labuschagne there does well to hang onto the ball and then, he falls onto the ground. Something to rejoice for Australia as the centurion of the first innings departs at the stroke of Stumps, cheaply.
Loopy ball on off, it is a touch too full. Hafeez times it to covers.
Flatter around off, Hafeez plays it onto the ground a little late.
Very full on the pads, the batsman works it to mid-wicket.
The arm ball on off, Hafeez pushes it towards covers.
It is on the pads, Imam flicks it fine down the leg side for a run. All too easy for Pakistan at the moment.
Uses his feet and eases it down to long on for a run.
Another offie on off, Hafeez lunges and keeps it out.
Fires it on off, MH blocks it out easily.
This one pitches in the rough outside off and comes back in sharply. Hafeez tries to defend but is hit high on the pads.
Flatter around off, it turns away. Imam goes to cut but the shot is not on. He chops it towards cover-point for a run.
Holland is a bit too straight and Imam helps himself by flicking it through square leg to get one more run.
Fires this on the leg stump line. The southpaw glances this fine into the leg side to get a single.
Slower and shorter outside off this, allows Hafeez to punch it through covers and get off strike.
Imam works this full ball on middle down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Changes his side and comes from around the wicket to the right-hander. Keeps this a bit short on off and Hafeez punches this to covers to take a single.
Slower and on middle turning into Imam, he goes back and works it with the spin into the square leg region to pick up a single and get off strike.
Jon Holland is brought into the attack.
A bit shorter this, punched to covers.
Beaten! Lovely bowling from Lyon. He bowls this a bit slower and a bit shorter than full length, Imam comes forward looking to defend but the ball spins away from him beating his outside edge.
A bit fuller this on off, Imam again comes forward and defends.
Slow loopy delivery on off, Imam lunges forward in defense.
Similar delivery but this time Imam goes back to defend it.
Flighted and full on middle and off, kept out off the front foot.
Errs in line and ends up bowling it down the leg side, the southpaw just tucks it towards fine leg and gets a run.
A tad fuller around off, Imam defends off the front foot.
Better from Peter as he lands this around a meter before the batsman, Imam blocks this from within the crease.
Dishes this a bit straighter and on the pads of the batsman, Imam flicks it through square leg to get a brace.
Similar ball, Imam shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Siddle from around the wicket fires in a good length delivery angling into Imam. It's around off, the southpaw defends it and gets down giving an impression that it kept a bit low.
Floats it up on off, Hafeez is solid in defense.
On the shorter side, Imam goes back and works it to mid-wicket for a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On the stumps, Imam lunges and keeps it out.
FOUR! Short, wide and it has been put away. Imam pounces on the poor delivery and cuts it through point and the ball races away.
Bowls it quicker on off, Imam goes back and defends it.
Inside edge! Fuller in length and shaping back in. Hafeez tries to drive but he gets an inside edge onto his pads. The players appeal but the umpire shakes his head.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Fuller in length on off, it is stroked to mid off.
Loose shot! Slightly short and outside off, Hafeez tries to cut it but gets beaten.
Fuller in length on middle, the batsman flicks it towards mid-wicket.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Peter SIddle comes into the attack now.
On the stumps, Imam is solid in defense.

Half chance there! We saw Imam defending the balls a little uppishly in the first innings and the same thing happened here. However, unlike the first innings there was a silly point this time. It goes aerially towards him but he fails to react in time. Would have been a brilliant take, had he taken it. Australia need all the chances that come their way to be taken.
On the stumps, it has been defended.
Flatter on off, Imam blocks it.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flatter on off, kept out.
A little bit of extra bounce there! On a length and around off, Hafeez is squared up as he tries to defend but somehow keeps it out.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Two good deliveries in a row! On a length and on off, defended.
Good delivery! On a length and around off, straightens a touch. MH blocks it off the back foot.
Misses his radar and bowls it very wide outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Take that! The right-hander is continuing from where he left off. On the shorter side outside off, Hafeez stands tall and punches it through covers for a boundary.

In the air... but safe! Hafeez tries to play the paddle sweep but gets a top edge. It goes up in the air towards the backward square leg fielder who runs to his right but does not get to it. A single taken.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Another loopy delivery on off, Hafeez keeps it out.
FOUR! Cracked! That has raced to the fence. Another off spinner from Lyon. Hafeez goes down on one knee and sweeps it hard through square leg. It is in the gap which means a boundary.

Just short but a lot of turn there. Lyon floats it up on off, it comes back in sharply. Takes the inside edge, hits the pads and lobs towards first slip. The fielder there puts in a dive forward but collects it on the bounce. Okay, hold on, the replays later show, even if the fielder had taken it, it would not have made a difference as it was off the pads.
Works it with the turn to the man at mid-wicket.
Goes for the yorker on middle, Hafeez jams it out towards covers for a run.
FOUR! Too easy! Short and wide outside off, it comes slow off the surface. Hafeez has all the time in the world to guide it through backward point and fetch a boundary.
Closer to the off pole this time, Hafeez punches it towards covers. He took off as he wanted a run but his partner sends him back in time. The fielder has a shy at the batsman's end but misses.
Another ball a little too wide outside off, the batsman shoulders arms to it.
Good length way outside off, left alone.
Fuller in length outside off, Hafeez tries to drive but it goes off the inner half towards the bowler.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Another shortish delivery on off, Imam punches it firmly to the man at covers.
Fires it outside off, turning away. Left alone.
Flatter in length on off, the batsman keeps it out.
FOUR! Cracked! Lyon drops it short and a bit outside off, Imam punches this through the cover-point region for the first boundary of this innings.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Hafeez lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Leg bye. Full but down the leg side, Imam looks to flick but misses the ball and gets hit on the pads. The batsmen take a single as the ball rolls in the gap behind the square leg region.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
A shorter in length delivery and on off, Imam tries to punch it but the ball seems to have stuck in this slow pitch. The ball gets the inner half of his bat and rolls towards square leg.
Fires this one straight in line with the stumps, the southpaw flicks it to square leg.
